Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 07/15/2026
Patient: Lance Quitzon, 68-year-old male

Lance Quitzon presents today with complaints related to his back. Reports back pain for about six months. He describes the pain as persistent and localized to the lower back without radiation. There is no history of recent trauma or injury. On examination, there is tenderness over the lumbar spine with mild limitation in range of motion due to discomfort. Neurological examination reveals intact sensation and motor strength in the lower extremities. Vital signs are stable. The assessment is chronic back pain likely of musculoskeletal origin without neurological deficits. The plan includes conservative management with physical therapy and use of over-the-counter analgesics as needed. The patient is advised to monitor symptoms and report any new neurological changes. A follow-up visit is scheduled in six weeks to evaluate progress.

Radiology Report
Date: 08/21/2026
Patient: Lance Quitzon, 68-year-old male

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 08/21/2026: acute osteoporotic L2 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the L2 vertebral body, demonstrated by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. No other acute abnormalities are identified.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the referring physician.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/03/2026
Patient: Lance Quitzon, 68-year-old male

History:
Back pain began 07/10/2026 after a fall from standing height, 8 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Pain NRS 8/10 despite 7 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has worsened over the past two weeks despite bracing.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current pain management and bracing. Consider interventional options based on further evaluation and patient response.
